title: Landmark decision taken by Government of India in Medical Education
author: Press Information Bureau
excerpt: PIB release announcing 27% OBC and 10% EWS reservation in the 15% All India Quota (AIQ) scheme for MBBS/BDS/MD/MS seats, effective from academic year 2021-22. It notes the AIQ scheme was introduced in 1986 on Supreme Court directions to give domicile-free, merit-based access to seats in other states. The government estimates roughly 1,500 OBC and 550 EWS students benefit in MBBS each year, ~5,550 across UG and PG.

title: MBBS entrance: Here's the complete guide to NEET 2026
author: MD Bureau
excerpt: A reference guide to NEET-UG 2026 conducted by the NTA, covering the exam date, application process, age and qualification eligibility, and the 180-question Physics/Chemistry/Biology paper structure. It also walks through what happens after the result: the counselling rounds, reservation policy, and admission criteria for MBBS, BDS and allied courses.

title: NEET UG, PG Counselling 2026-27: MCC notifies criteria for candidates seeking nationality conversion to NRI
author: Divyani Paul
excerpt: The Medical Counselling Committee has notified who actually qualifies for an NRI-quota seat in 2026-27, applying the Supreme Court's guidance on the subject. Eligibility turns on a parent or first-degree relative genuinely being an NRI resident abroad, backed by affidavits, relationship certificates and sponsorship proof. It is a useful corrective for families who assume an NRI sponsor can be arranged at the last minute.

title: 148 EWS category students take around Rs 1 crore Management, NRI quota seats, NMC calls for state-level probe
author: Barsha Misra
excerpt: The NMC has ordered a state-level investigation after 148 students holding EWS certificates were found taking management and NRI quota medical seats costing up to roughly Rs 1 crore. The contradiction raises questions about fraudulent EWS certificates and undisclosed funding. A cautionary read on how the high-fee quota route actually works.

title: Reasonable accommodation not charity but fundamental right, SC rules, grants MBBS seat to disabled aspirant
author: Khadija Khan
excerpt: The Supreme Court ordered AIIMS Delhi to admit Kabir Paharia, a NEET-qualified candidate with locomotor disability, under the SC-PwBD quota. The bench held that reasonable accommodation is a fundamental right rather than charity, and that a minor functional difficulty cannot disqualify an otherwise capable candidate. It directed the NMC to revise its disability eligibility guidelines.

title: 80% foreign medical graduates fail India's licence exam. Here's what they end up doing instead
author: Kritika Sharma and Abantika Ghosh
excerpt: Graduates of MBBS programmes in countries such as Russia, China, Ukraine and the Philippines must clear the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) to practise in India, and on average about 80% fail. The report follows students who have attempted the exam repeatedly and moved into hospital management and other non-clinical work.

title: After flip flops on NExT, NMC now seeks public feedback on the medical test's feasibility
author: Sumi Sukanya Dutta
excerpt: The National Medical Commission issued a public notice asking stakeholders whether the National Exit Test can realistically replace final-year MBBS exams, NEET-PG and the FMGE. The NMC had announced and then withdrawn multiple NExT timelines after protests from students and intervention by the health ministry.

title: More than 37,000 Medicos respond to NMC survey, confirm Suffering from Mental Health Issues
author: Barsha Misra
excerpt: Over 37,000 medical students and faculty responded to a National Medical Commission mental-health survey, documenting widespread distress in medical education. The NMC recorded 122 student suicides between 2018 and 2023 alongside 1,270 dropouts, and recommended capped duty hours, gatekeeper training and round-the-clock counselling.

title: Doctors welcome MP's decision to scrap seat-leaving bond for MBBS students. What the policy entails
author: Sumi Sukanya Dutta
excerpt: Madhya Pradesh became the first state to scrap its seat-leaving bond, which had required MBBS students to pay Rs 30 lakh to leave a course midway. Doctors' bodies welcomed the move, while defenders argue bonds secure rural postings and prevent seat wastage in subsidised colleges.

title: Variation in training may lead to disqualification! NMC warns students planning MBBS abroad
author: Garima
excerpt: The NMC warned aspirants that foreign medical degrees not matching its standards can be refused registration in India. Under the Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations 2021, the course must run 54 months, be taught in English, include a 12-month internship abroad plus one in India, and be followed by the exit exam.

title: 'Study medicine without practicals': Tough road for Indians enrolled in China as visa ban stays
author: Kritika Sharma
excerpt: Roughly 23,000 Indian students, mostly medical, were stranded in India after China's pandemic-era visa ban, completing large parts of their MBBS online. Without clinical rotations or hands-on practicals, they struggled to secure internships and to qualify for the FMGE required to practise in India.

title: Cabinet approves major expansion of postgraduate and undergraduate medical education capacity in the country
author: Press Information Bureau
excerpt: The Union Cabinet approved Phase-III of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme to upgrade existing government medical colleges and PG institutes, adding 5,000 PG seats and 5,023 MBBS seats. The combined outlay is Rs 15,034.50 crore for 2025-26 to 2028-29.

title: India's first dengue vaccine has been in the making for 17 yrs. DengiAll has the world excited
author: Akanksha Mishra
excerpt: Panacea Biotec, with ICMR support, completed Phase-III trials of DengiAll, India's first indigenous dengue vaccine, enrolling over 10,000 participants across 20 sites. It uses attenuated strains targeting all four dengue serotypes equally in a single dose, addressing antibody-dependent enhancement.

title: ICMR Licenses Nine Breakthrough Health Technologies to Industry Partners at India MedTech Expo 2025
author: Press Information Bureau
excerpt: At India MedTech Expo 2025, ICMR licensed nine technologies to industry partners under its Medical Innovations-Patent Mitra initiative, producing 17 licensing deals. The innovations span infectious disease diagnostics, immunodiagnostics and vaccine development.

title: India's 'doctor shortage' narrative overshadows the neglect of public health
author: Kiran Kumbhar
excerpt: Physician-historian Kiran Kumbhar argues there is a policymaking blindspot that equates better health outcomes with a larger supply of doctors. He contends that the dominant 'doctor shortage' framing crowds out investment in public health systems, prevention and primary care.

title: Rural India has an 80% shortfall of specialist doctors. MP, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu worst off
author: Sumi Sukanya Dutta
excerpt: Per the Rural Health Statistics / Health Dynamics 2022-23 report, rural community health centres have only 4,413 of the 21,964 specialist doctors they need, an ~80% shortfall. Madhya Pradesh's deficit runs to about 94%.
